changelog.summary: Evolve of mcp_builder from v1.1.0 to v2.0.0: NN12 SSRF egress tightened from block-private-IP to ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny). BREAKING — a v1.1.0-conformant server whose outbound-fetch path only blocked private/loopback/link-local ranges while defaulting to allowing undeclared public URLs is NO LONGER conformant: NN12 now requires that only explicitly-declared allow-list hosts may egress and every undeclared host is blocked. Scope-bounded: ONLY the SSRF/egress red line + its assert + template guidance changed; NN11 auth-presence and all other v1.1.0 red lines/capabilities preserved byte-for-byte.
breaks: NN12 (ReviewTest.step6:sys.assert) egress predicate flipped from 'explicit allow-list check AND private-IP/link-local/loopback block' (which still admitted default-allow public egress) to ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny): the accept-set of conformant servers SHRINKS. Any generated server relying on default-public-egress with a private-range-only guard must be regenerated with an explicit static allow-list that fails closed on undeclared hosts.

system_prompt, ResearchPlan.step3 planning guidance, discovery.guidance SSRF item, summary and description were re-worded to the allow-list-only (default-deny) policy so the generated MCP server template/guidance stops steering builders toward a block-private-ranges-only fetch path.
changes: A1 (LEVEL_A): NN12 red line rule text rewritten from 'validated against an explicit allow-list AND private-IP/link-local/loopback egress blocked' to ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) — only statically-declared allow-list hosts may egress, every undeclared host is blocked, NO default public egress; private/loopback/link-local ranges remain blocked as a subset of the default-deny posture. A block-private-ranges-only guard that otherwise reaches the public internet is now REJECTED.

A2 (LEVEL_A): NN12 enforcement assert at ReviewTest.step6 tightened — the sys.assert predicate now requires a default-deny allow-list gate (explicit allow-list membership check that rejects undeclared hosts); a fetch path permitting arbitrary public URLs, or one that only blocks private/loopback/link-local ranges but defaults to allowing undeclared public hosts, now FAILS the assertion.

A3 (SEMVER): deliberate MAJOR v1.1.0 -> v2.0.0 with explicit breaks[] per ENFORCED_BY_PREDICATE_FLIP — the NN12 predicate flip shrinks the conformant accept-set (a v1.1.0-compliant default-public-egress server becomes non-conformant), a breaking change, NOT self-adjudicated as MINOR.
C1: prose sync — system_prompt SSRF clause, aisp_contract.discovery.guidance SSRF item, summary and description synchronized to the allow-list-only (default-deny) egress policy.

C2: generated MCP server template/guidance sync — ResearchPlan.step3 outbound-fetch planning directive and ReviewTest.constraints NN12 description synchronized so the scaffolded server template steers builders to an explicit static allow-list / default-deny fetch path (no default-public-egress plan).

C3: SKILL.md + README.md sidecars deterministically re-derived from the updated aisp_contract (aisp_skill_md.py / aisp_readme.py) so the discovery bridge and README project the new NN12 allow-list-only policy and version 2.0.0.
C4: version + metadata sync — version 1.1.0 -> 2.0.0; changelog MAJOR entry with breaks[]; summary/description/system_prompt/non_negotiable NN12/discovery.guidance synchronized.

BOUNDARY FREEZE: NN11 auth-presence (ReviewTest.step5) and NN1/NN5/NN6/NN7/NN8/NN9/NN10 preserved byte-for-byte (NN8 next_offset offset-pagination clause intact); the four non-deterministic-threat guidance items, all non-SSRF v1.1.0 capabilities, and the four-phase topology unchanged.

content.summary: AISP V1.0.0 skill that guides building MCP servers in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript SDK via the four-phase flow Research-and-Plan -> Implement -> Review-and-Test -> Create-Evaluations, producing a server plus a read-only evaluation suite. Nine sys.assert/tools-bound non-negotiable rules cover strict schemas, tool annotations, actionable errors, offset pagination, no-stdout-on-stdio, read-only evals, open-world docs, http-auth presence, and allow-list-only (default-deny) SSRF egress.
content.description: mcp_builder is a guidance and code-generation skill for authoring MCP servers. Given a target external service/API it (1) researches modern MCP design and loads protocol + SDK docs on demand via web_fetch (the external MCP/SDK docs are open-world, fetched at runtime, never bundled as static skill content), (2) lets the builder choose Python FastMCP or Node TypeScript SDK at a real decision node, (3) scaffolds the server with strict input schemas (Pydantic extra='forbid' / Zod .strict()), four annotation hints per tool, centralized actionable error handling, and limit/has_more/next_offset pagination, (4) reviews and builds/compiles the server and tests with MCP Inspector, and (5) authors ten complex, read-only, string-verifiable evaluation questions emitted as evaluation XML. The skill distilled nine non_negotiable red lines from the largely-implicit directives of the upstream Anthropic mcp-builder skill, each bound to a concrete sys.assert structural/grammar check or to the restricted tools allow-list — including a structural-presence assert that http/remote transport declares an auth section (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + token-audience guidance) and a deterministic allow-list-only (default-deny) SSRF-egress assert on outbound fetch (only explicitly-declared hosts may egress; undeclared hosts blocked; no default public egress; private/loopback/link-local ranges blocked as a subset) — and is honest that the annotation hints are not security guarantees and that prompt-injection / tool-poisoning / confused-deputy / token-passthrough remain LLM-judgement guidance, not fake asserts. It writes only the generated server + evaluation files and treats its bundled reference docs as read-only. References modern MCP practice against the 2025-11-25 spec (noting the 2026-07-28 Release Candidate), Streamable HTTP transport with the SSE-deprecation warning, and the SEP-2577 deprecation of Sampling/Roots/Logging.

tool_annotations._note: These four annotation fields (readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint) are HINTS, NOT security guarantees (MCP 2026 spec + reference/mcp_best_practices.md L201). A client MUST NOT make a security-critical decision based solely on an annotation; absent annotations default pessimistically (non-read-only, potentially destructive, non-idempotent, open-world). openWorldHint=true is a declaration that the capability interacts with an open world of external entities (the internet / third-party APIs), not an enforced boundary.

file_system.note: Reads the bundled read-only reference docs and writes ONLY the generated MCP server files + evaluation XML into the build workspace. Never modifies its own source_material.

web_search.note: Used in Phase 1 to discover current MCP / SDK / target-API documentation. Open-world: queries the public internet.

web_fetch.note: On-demand runtime fetch of external MCP spec pages (modelcontextprotocol.io .md), python-sdk README, and typescript-sdk README. These external docs are open-world and fetched at runtime, NOT laundered into static bundled files.

code.note: Local build/compile only: `npm run build` / `python -m py_compile` and the MCP Inspector smoke test against the generated server. No network egress from the build step itself.

params.service_api: string, REQUIRED: identity/description of the external service or API the MCP server should wrap (name, base URL, auth model, key endpoints). Drives tool selection in ResearchPlan.
params.language: string, default: 'auto'. Builder language preference consumed by the LangSelect decision node: 'python' -> ImplementPy (FastMCP), 'node'/'typescript' -> ImplementNode (TS SDK), 'auto' -> recommend TypeScript per reference guidance but let the builder confirm. LangSelect remains a real decision branch, not a silent parameter.
params.transport: string, default: 'stdio'. Target transport: 'stdio' for local servers (no stdout logging — use stderr), 'http' for remote servers using Streamable HTTP (stateless JSON; per MCP 2025-11-25 the older HTTP+SSE transport is DEPRECATED — do NOT scaffold a standalone SSE endpoint, prefer Streamable HTTP). Remote/http transport MUST declare an auth section (see NN11).
params.tool_budget: integer, default: 12. Soft cap on the number of tools to implement in the first pass; prioritizes the most common operations for comprehensive coverage.
params.eval_count: integer, default: 10. Number of evaluation questions to author in Phase 4 (the upstream skill specifies 10 complex, independent, read-only, string-verifiable, stable questions).
params.build_workspace: string, REQUIRED: absolute or workspace-relative directory where the generated MCP server source + evaluation.xml are written. The skill writes ONLY here; it never modifies its own bundled reference docs.

json_schema.description: mcp_builder output: a generated MCP server plan/artifact set plus a read-only evaluation suite.

content.system_prompt:
You guide the construction of high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). STRICTLY OBEY aisp_contract: its nine non_negotiable rules are inviolable and each is bound to a real enforcement mechanism (sys.assert structural/grammar checks or the restricted tools allow-list). Follow the four-phase flow Research-and-Plan -> (choose language) -> Implement -> Review-and-Test -> Create-Evaluations. Every tool you generate MUST declare the four annotation hints and a strict input schema (Pydantic extra='forbid' / Zod .strict()); errors MUST be actionable and returned in result objects; list tools MUST paginate with limit + has_more + next_offset; stdio servers MUST log to stderr, never stdout; evaluation questions MUST be read-only, idempotent, and string-verifiable. When the target transport is http/remote, the server MUST declare an auth section (OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + mandatory PKCE(S256) + token-audience validation per RFC 8707/RFC 9068; never pass a raw client token through to upstream APIs) and any LLM-provided fetch URL MUST pass an ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) SSRF egress policy — only hosts on the server's explicit allow-list may egress, every undeclared host is blocked (no default public egress), and private/loopback/link-local ranges stay blocked as a subset. Treat the four annotation hints as HINTS, not security guarantees; and treat prompt-injection, tool-poisoning, confused-deputy, and token-passthrough as risks you must warn about with LLM judgement, not as deterministically enforced asserts. Load external MCP/SDK docs on demand via web_fetch at runtime against the 2025-11-25 spec (note the 2026-07-28 Release Candidate) and prefer Streamable HTTP over the deprecated HTTP+SSE transport; never bundle those docs as static skill content. Mirror the user's exact language and script variant in narrative output.
Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing.

content.instruction: STRICTLY OBEY aisp_contract; its non_negotiable rules are inviolable and bound to real enforcement mechanisms; then RUN aisop.main.

when_to_use: The user wants to build an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets an LLM call an external service or API through well-designed tools.
The user is writing an MCP server in Python with FastMCP or in Node/TypeScript with the MCP SDK and wants the recommended structure, strict input schemas, annotations, error handling, and pagination.
The user wants the full MCP-builder workflow: research/plan the tools, implement the server, review and build/test it, and create an evaluation suite.
The user needs to author MCP evaluation questions (read-only, complex, string-verifiable) and emit them as evaluation XML.
The user wants to wrap a documented REST/HTTP API as MCP tools with correct readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint annotations.
when_not_to_use: The user wants generic (non-MCP) application or API code generation with no MCP server involved.
The user wants to run destructive or state-mutating operations against a live MCP server's backend as part of evaluation (evaluations here are strictly read-only / non-destructive).
The user wants to operate, monitor, or deploy an already-running production MCP server rather than author a new one.
The user wants the external MCP/SDK documentation bundled as static offline content rather than fetched on demand (these docs are open-world / runtime-fetched).
The user wants the skill to modify its own bundled reference documents or any source material (the references are read-only).

non_negotiable.rule: NN1 — Evaluation questions MUST be read-only, non-destructive, and idempotent: every authored qa_pair may only require tool calls whose readOnlyHint=true / destructiveHint=false, and any qa_pair that would require a WRITE or DESTRUCTIVE operation is dropped. Source: reference/evaluation.md (questions must require only non-destructive and idempotent tool use; verification step flags and removes any qa_pair requiring write/destructive operations).

NN5 — Tool/API errors MUST be actionable: the generated server returns helpful, specific error messages with a suggested next step INSIDE the result object (isError), never throwing raw exceptions and never leaking internal implementation details. Source: SKILL.md (error messages should guide agents toward solutions with specific suggestions and next steps) + reference/mcp_best_practices.md L206-211.

NN6 — Every tool MUST declare all four annotation hints (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) as booleans. This is a STRUCTURAL presence + boolean-type check, NOT a proof of semantic truthfulness — the annotations are hints, not security guarantees. Source: SKILL.md L119-124 + reference/mcp_best_practices.md L60/L190-201.

NN7 — Tool input validation MUST use a strict schema: Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='forbid') in Python or Zod .strict() in TypeScript, forbidding extra fields; ad-hoc hand-written if-checks are rejected. Source: reference/python_mcp_server.md (Pydantic models handle input validation, ConfigDict extra='forbid') + reference/node_mcp_server.md (Zod .strict() to forbid extra fields) + reference/mcp_best_practices.md L172.

NN8 — List/collection tools MUST paginate: respect the limit parameter and return has_more and next_offset (plus total_count). next_offset is the tool-RESULT offset pagination convention faithful to reference/mcp_best_practices.md L20-23 / L84-104; it is a DISTINCT layer from the MCP protocol-transport opaque cursor (nextCursor) and MUST NOT be rewritten to nextCursor.

NN9 — stdio servers MUST NOT log to stdout: stdout is the JSON-RPC channel, so all logging goes to stderr (Python logging->stderr, Node console.error, never console.log/print on the stdio transport path). Source: reference/mcp_best_practices.md L139 + reference/node_mcp_server.md (console.error for stdio logging).

NN10 — External MCP/SDK documentation is ON-DEMAND / OPEN-WORLD: it is fetched at runtime via web_fetch (modelcontextprotocol.io spec pages, python-sdk README, typescript-sdk README) and is NEVER bundled as static skill content. The skill therefore declares web_search/web_fetch with openWorldHint=true and marks those external URLs as open_world/runtime, not as static read_only resources. Source: SKILL.md L41-43/L61/L65/L203/L212-213.

NN11 — When transport is http/remote, the generated server MUST declare an authorization section: a STRUCTURAL presence + type check that an auth/authorization block exists on the http/remote transport path (i.e. it is NOT left unauthenticated). This is presence-only, mirroring NN6's framing — it verifies the auth section is PRESENT and structured, NOT that the auth is cryptographically correct or unbypassable (no semantic security guarantee). For stdio transport the check is vacuously satisfied (no network auth surface). The recommended shape (OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + mandatory PKCE(S256) + token-audience validation per RFC 8707/RFC 9068, and no raw client-token passthrough to upstream APIs) lives in discovery.guidance; this red line only asserts the presence of the section, not its semantic strength. Source: MCP 2025-11-25 authorization spec + reference/mcp_best_practices.md.

NN12 — Outbound fetch MUST be SSRF-safe under an ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) egress policy: any LLM-provided / user-provided URL the generated server would fetch MUST be validated against an explicit, statically-declared allow-list, and ONLY hosts on that allow-list may egress — every undeclared host is blocked (default-deny). There is NO default public-internet egress: an outbound-fetch path that permits arbitrary public URLs so long as private/loopback/link-local ranges are blocked is REJECTED, because blocking private ranges alone still leaves the whole public internet reachable. Private / loopback / link-local egress remains blocked as before, but is now a subset of the default-deny posture rather than the whole guarantee. This is a DETERMINISTICALLY assertable structural check over the emitted server (a default-deny allow-list gate is present on the outbound-fetch path: the URL host is checked against an explicit allow-list and rejected when absent). The non-deterministic threats — prompt-injection, tool-poisoning, confused-deputy, and token-passthrough — are NOT asserted here; they remain LLM-judgement guidance in discovery.guidance with no fabricated enforced_by. Source: MCP 2026 security best practices + reference/mcp_best_practices.md security section + OWASP SSRF default-deny allow-list guidance.

external_docs._note: These are OPEN-WORLD, RUNTIME-FETCHED external documents (NN10). They are intentionally NOT listed in aisp_contract.resources because they are not bundled static files — they are fetched on demand via the open_world web_fetch capability. Marked honestly as open_world/runtime; never laundered into static read_only resources.

open_world_runtime.url: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/sitemap.xml (then fetch specific spec pages with .md suffix; anchor on the 2025-11-25 formal spec e.g. /specification/2025-11-25.md and note the 2026-07-28 Release Candidate)
https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization.md (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + resource-indicator / token-audience guidance behind NN11)

guidance._note: These directives from the upstream mcp-builder skill are LLM-judgement-only quality guidance. They are deliberately NOT promoted to non_negotiable because no deterministic enforced_by mechanism can verify them; fabricating a sys.assert for them would be dishonest. The auth-scheme details behind NN11 and the non-deterministic security threats adjacent to NN12 (prompt-injection / tool-poisoning / confused-deputy / token-passthrough) live HERE as guidance, precisely because they require semantic/LLM judgement rather than a deterministic structural assert.
items: DRY: avoid duplicated code; factor shared API-client / formatting / error helpers (reference/mcp_best_practices.md, SKILL.md Phase 3.1).
Comprehensive API coverage: when uncertain, prioritize comprehensive endpoint coverage over narrow workflow tools (SKILL.md Phase 1.1).
Realistic, complex evaluation questions: each question should reflect a real use case requiring multiple tool calls and deep exploration (reference/evaluation.md, SKILL.md Phase 4.3).
Clear, action-oriented tool naming with consistent service prefixes, e.g. github_create_issue (SKILL.md Phase 1.1, reference/mcp_best_practices.md naming section).

STRUCTURED OUTPUT (strengthened, LEVEL_B): PREFER defining outputSchema + returning structuredContent for every tool that returns structured data — do NOT treat this as optional 'where possible' boilerplate; a tool that returns machine-parseable data without a declared outputSchema is a quality smell to flag in ReviewTest. This is guidance-strengthening only and is intentionally NOT a hard sys.assert red line (it is not deterministically enforceable across all tool shapes). Source: MCP 2025-11-25 tool outputSchema, SKILL.md Phase 2.3.

AUTH (behind NN11, http/remote transport): use OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow with MANDATORY PKCE(S256); validate the access-token audience (resource indicator) per RFC 8707 and treat tokens as JWT access tokens per RFC 9068 where applicable; the MCP server acts as an OAuth Resource Server and MUST NOT pass a raw client/user token straight through to the upstream third-party API (no token passthrough / confused-deputy). NN11 only asserts the auth section is structurally PRESENT; the correctness of this scheme is LLM-judgement guidance. Source: MCP 2025-11-25 authorization spec, OAuth 2.1 draft, RFC 8707 / RFC 9068.

SSRF / non-deterministic security (adjacent to NN12): the deterministic red line NN12 now asserts an ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) egress gate — only explicitly-declared hosts may be fetched, every undeclared host is blocked, there is NO default public egress, and private/loopback/link-local ranges stay blocked as a subset of that default-deny posture. When implementing an outbound-fetch path, maintain the allow-list as an explicit static declaration and fail closed on any host not on it; do NOT fall back to a block-private-ranges-only guard that still reaches the whole public internet. Two implementation notes make the allow-list gate robust against runtime bypass (guidance only — these are runtime behaviors that cannot be deterministically verified at scaffold time, so they are NOT promoted to a sys.assert): (a) DNS-rebinding / TOCTOU — enforce the allow-list on the RESOLVED IP at connection time (IP pinning: resolve once, then connect to that pinned IP, ideally via a single-resolve-and-connect egress proxy), not on the hostname string alone; otherwise a rebinding domain passes the host allow-list check and then resolves to a private / metadata IP (e.g. 169.254.169.254, RFC1918) at fetch time. (b) redirect-following — disable automatic redirect following OR re-validate the final resolved IP against the allow-list on every hop; otherwise a trusted allow-listed host that exposes an open redirect can bounce the request to an undeclared or private target and bypass the gate. Beyond that asserted gate, exercise LLM judgement against prompt-injection (untrusted content in tool inputs/outputs steering the agent), tool-poisoning (malicious tool descriptions/annotations — remember annotations are hints, not guarantees), confused-deputy (the server being tricked into using its own credentials on the caller's behalf), and token-passthrough (never forward an inbound token to a downstream service). These non-deterministic threats are NOT asserted — they have no honest deterministic enforced_by. Source: MCP 2026 security best practices, OWASP Agentic AI Top-10, OWASP SSRF Prevention (allow-list / default-deny).

SPEC & TRANSPORT CURRENCY: research against the MCP 2025-11-25 formal specification (note the 2026-07-28 Release Candidate: stateless protocol core, Tasks SEP-2663, the formal deprecation policy SEP-2577); prefer the Streamable HTTP transport and warn that the older HTTP+SSE transport is DEPRECATED (do not scaffold a standalone SSE endpoint). Source: modelcontextprotocol.io spec (2025-11-25 + 2026-07-28 RC), SKILL.md Phase 1.

DEPRECATION AWARENESS (SEP-2577): the Sampling, Roots, and Logging primitives are deprecated per SEP-2577 — generated servers should avoid building on to-be-removed primitives; this is direction-consistent with NN9 (stdio logging routed to stderr, not the client-side Logging capability). Source: MCP SEP-2577 deprecation policy.

aisop.main:
graph TD
    ResearchPlan[Phase1: research MCP design + load docs on-demand + plan tools] --> LangSelect{Python FastMCP or Node TS SDK?}
    LangSelect --> ImplementPy[Phase2 Python: FastMCP scaffold + Pydantic extra=forbid + 4 annotations]
    LangSelect --> ImplementNode[Phase2 Node: TS SDK scaffold + Zod .strict + 4 annotations]
    ImplementPy --> ReviewTest[Phase3: DRY/type review + build/compile + MCP Inspector]
    ImplementNode --> ReviewTest
    ReviewTest --> EvalGen[Phase4: 10 read-only string-verifiable eval questions then XML]
    EvalGen --> ReportDeliver[Assemble server + evaluation.xml + quality checklist]
    ReportDeliver --> endNode((End))

ResearchPlan.step1: [ASSERT] Valid invocation received. Required: service_api, build_workspace. | PHASE 1 — DEEP RESEARCH & PLANNING. Understand modern MCP design: balance comprehensive API-endpoint coverage against specialized workflow tools (when uncertain, prioritize comprehensive coverage); plan clear, action-oriented tool names with a consistent service prefix; plan concise descriptions and pagination/filtering for context management.
ResearchPlan.step2: Load documentation ON-DEMAND (open-world): use web_search to find current MCP guidance, then web_fetch the MCP spec from https://modelcontextprotocol.io/sitemap.xml (fetch specific pages with the .md suffix) — anchor on the 2025-11-25 FORMAL specification and note the 2026-07-28 Release Candidate (stateless protocol core, Tasks SEP-2663, the SEP-2577 deprecation policy) — plus the python-sdk README and the typescript-sdk README. Read the bundled read-only references reference/mcp_best_practices.md (universal guidelines) for naming/format/pagination/transport/security/error/annotation conventions. These external docs are runtime-fetched and never bundled as static content (NN10).
ResearchPlan.step3: Plan the implementation: review the target service_api's endpoints, auth model, and data models (web_search + web_fetch as needed); select the tool set up to tool_budget, starting with the most common operations; decide transport — stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote (the older HTTP+SSE transport is DEPRECATED per MCP 2025-11-25, so do NOT plan a standalone SSE endpoint). For an http/remote transport, plan an authorization section up front (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + token-audience validation — see NN11 / discovery.guidance) and an ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) SSRF egress policy for any outbound fetch of LLM-provided URLs: enumerate the explicit set of hosts the server is permitted to reach and reject every undeclared host — do NOT plan a default-public-egress fetch path that merely blocks private ranges (NN12); plan to enforce the allow-list on the RESOLVED IP at connection time (IP pinning / single-resolve-and-connect egress proxy, not a hostname-string check that a DNS-rebinding domain can defeat) and to disable automatic redirect following (or re-validate the final resolved IP against the allow-list on every hop) so an open redirect on a trusted host cannot bounce to an undeclared target. Emit a tool plan + chosen recommended language hint to LangSelect.
ResearchPlan.constraints: Phase 1 is read-and-plan only: no server code is written here. External MCP/SDK docs are fetched on demand via web_fetch (open_world) and are NOT copied into the skill as static files. The bundled reference docs are opened read-only and never modified.
ResearchPlan.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(proceed with bundled references only + UNVERIFIED_DOCS note) -> inform(User). Error types: io_error(doc_fetch_failure)->retry(1) then fallback to bundled references. validation_failure(missing_service_api)->no retry, reject. timeout(search_timeout)->retry with backoff then fallback.

LangSelect.step1: [ASSERT] ResearchPlan executed. Required: tool plan, recommended language hint. | DECISION NODE — choose the implementation stack. Read the `language` param: 'python' -> route to ImplementPy (FastMCP); 'node'/'typescript' -> route to ImplementNode (TS SDK); 'auto' -> recommend TypeScript (high-quality SDK support, strong static typing/linting, broad model familiarity per reference framework guidance) and confirm the choice with the builder before branching.
LangSelect.step2: Bind the chosen language into the build context and route to exactly ONE implementation branch (ImplementPy XOR ImplementNode). Carry the tool plan, transport, and tool_budget into the selected branch.
LangSelect.constraints: This is a real decision node, not a silent parameter: exactly one of ImplementPy / ImplementNode runs per invocation. The recommendation is advisory; the builder's explicit `language` choice wins.
LangSelect.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(default to TypeScript/ImplementNode per recommended stack) -> inform(User). Error types: validation_failure(ambiguous_language)->resolve via recommendation default. timeout(decision_timeout)->fallback to recommended TypeScript.

ImplementPy.step1: [ASSERT] LangSelect executed (python branch). Required: tool plan, transport. | PHASE 2 (Python/FastMCP) — set up project structure (module organization, dependencies) and core infrastructure: an authenticated API client, error-handling helpers, response formatting (JSON/Markdown), and pagination support. Follow reference/python_mcp_server.md.
ImplementPy.step2: Implement each planned tool with @mcp.tool: a Pydantic BaseModel input schema with clear field descriptions and examples, async/await for I/O, an outputSchema/structuredContent where possible, and a concise description. Wire centralized actionable error handling (an _handle_api_error helper returning a helpful message + next step inside the result object).
ImplementPy.step3: sys.assert(every registered tool declares all four annotation hints — readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint — present and of boolean type in its @mcp.tool(annotations=...) block; this is a STRUCTURAL presence + type check, NOT a semantic guarantee that the tool truly is read-only) -> enforces NN6. A tool missing any of the four annotation keys, or with a non-boolean value, fails the assertion and the tool definition is rejected.
ImplementPy.step4: sys.assert(every tool input model is a Pydantic BaseModel with model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid'); reject any tool that validates input with ad-hoc hand-written if-checks instead of a strict schema) -> enforces NN7. Then hand the assembled Python server (with its tools + strict schemas + annotations + error helper) to ReviewTest.
ImplementPy.constraints: Python branch only. All tool inputs use Pydantic with extra='forbid' (no manual validation). All four annotations declared per tool. Errors are actionable and returned in result objects, never raised as raw exceptions. For stdio transport, logging goes to stderr only.
ImplementPy.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(emit partial server + record unimplemented tools) -> inform(User). Error types: assertion_error(missing_annotation|non_strict_schema)->no retry, reject the offending tool with guidance. parse_error(invalid_python)->retry(1) then partial. timeout(scaffold_timeout)->retry with backoff.

ImplementNode.step1: [ASSERT] LangSelect executed (node branch). Required: tool plan, transport. | PHASE 2 (Node/TypeScript SDK) — set up project structure (package.json, tsconfig.json) and core infrastructure: an authenticated API client, error-handling helpers, response formatting, and pagination support. Follow reference/node_mcp_server.md.
ImplementNode.step2: Implement each planned tool with server.registerTool: a Zod input schema, async/await for I/O, outputSchema/structuredContent where possible, and a concise description. Wire centralized actionable error handling (a handleApiError helper returning a helpful message + next step inside the result object).
ImplementNode.step3: sys.assert(every registered tool declares all four annotation hints — readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint — present and of boolean type in its registerTool annotations; STRUCTURAL presence + type check, NOT a semantic guarantee) -> enforces NN6 on the Node branch. A tool missing any of the four keys, or with a non-boolean value, fails and is rejected.
ImplementNode.step4: sys.assert(every tool input schema is a Zod object terminated with .strict() so extra fields are forbidden; reject any tool that hand-rolls input validation instead of a strict Zod schema) -> enforces NN7 on the Node branch. Then hand the assembled TypeScript server to ReviewTest.
ImplementNode.constraints: Node/TypeScript branch only. All tool inputs use Zod .strict() (no manual validation). All four annotations declared per tool. Errors are actionable and returned in result objects, never thrown raw. For stdio transport, logging uses console.error only (never console.log).
ImplementNode.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(emit partial server + record unimplemented tools) -> inform(User). Error types: assertion_error(missing_annotation|non_strict_schema)->no retry, reject the offending tool with guidance. parse_error(invalid_typescript)->retry(1) then partial. timeout(scaffold_timeout)->retry with backoff.

ReviewTest.step1: [ASSERT] ImplementPy or ImplementNode executed. Required: assembled server, transport. | PHASE 3 — CODE QUALITY REVIEW: review the generated server for DRY (no duplicated code), consistent error handling, full type coverage, and clear tool descriptions. BUILD & TEST: TypeScript -> `npm run build` to verify compilation; Python -> `python -m py_compile <server>.py`; then smoke-test with the MCP Inspector (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`).
ReviewTest.step2: sys.assert(the server routes tool/API failures through a centralized actionable error handler that returns a specific message + a suggested next step INSIDE the result object with isError set, and never leaks a raw stack trace or internal implementation detail) -> enforces NN5. A tool that throws raw exceptions or returns an opaque/internal error fails the assertion.
ReviewTest.step3: sys.assert(every list/collection tool respects the limit parameter and its response object contains has_more and next_offset keys (plus total_count); next_offset is the tool-result offset convention and MUST NOT be rewritten to the protocol-transport cursor nextCursor) -> enforces NN8. A list tool missing limit handling or the has_more/next_offset keys fails.
ReviewTest.step4: sys.assert(for stdio transport, no logging is written to stdout — Python logging is directed to stderr and Node uses console.error, never console.log/print on the stdio path, because stdout is the JSON-RPC channel) -> enforces NN9. Any stdout write on the stdio logging path fails the assertion.
ReviewTest.step5: sys.assert(when the target transport is http/remote, the generated server declares an auth/authorization section on the transport path — the section is STRUCTURALLY PRESENT and of the expected shape, i.e. the server is not left unauthenticated; for stdio transport this assertion is vacuously satisfied because there is no network auth surface) -> enforces NN11. This is a STRUCTURAL presence + type check ONLY, NOT a semantic proof that the auth is correct or unbypassable — the recommended OAuth 2.1 + PKCE(S256) + token-audience (RFC 8707/9068) + no-token-passthrough shape is guidance (discovery.guidance), and this assertion merely verifies the auth section is present. An http/remote server with no auth section fails the assertion.
ReviewTest.step6: sys.assert(every outbound-fetch path that consumes an LLM-provided or user-provided URL enforces an ALLOW-LIST-ONLY (default-deny) egress policy — the URL host is validated against an explicit, statically-declared allow-list and ONLY allow-listed hosts may egress while every undeclared host is blocked; there is NO default public egress; private / loopback / link-local ranges also remain blocked as a subset of the default-deny posture) -> enforces NN12. This is a DETERMINISTIC structural check that a default-deny allow-list gate is present on the fetch path (an explicit allow-list membership check that rejects undeclared hosts). A fetch path that permits arbitrary public URLs — including one that only blocks private/loopback/link-local ranges but otherwise defaults to allowing undeclared public hosts — FAILS the assertion, because default-allow public egress is no longer permitted. It does NOT assert the non-deterministic threats prompt-injection / tool-poisoning / confused-deputy / token-passthrough, which stay as LLM-judgement guidance (discovery.guidance) with no fabricated enforced_by. Pass the build_check + reviewed server to EvalGen.
ReviewTest.constraints: Phase 3 verifies the generated server, it does not author evaluations. The five assertions (NN5/NN8/NN9/NN11/NN12) are grammar/code-presence checks over the emitted server source: NN5/NN8/NN9 over error/pagination/logging, NN11 over the http/remote auth-section presence (structural only), NN12 over the outbound-fetch allow-list-only (default-deny) egress gate — only allow-listed hosts may egress, undeclared hosts are blocked, no default public egress, private/loopback/link-local ranges also blocked as a subset. Build/compile and the MCP Inspector smoke test run via the `code` capability locally.
ReviewTest.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(report failing checks + proceed to EvalGen with PARTIAL) -> inform(User). Error types: assertion_error(non_actionable_error|missing_pagination|stdout_logging|missing_http_auth_section|missing_ssrf_guard)->no retry, surface the violation for fix. command_error(build_failure)->retry(1) then PARTIAL with diagnostics. timeout(build_timeout|inspector_timeout)->retry with backoff.

EvalGen.step1: [ASSERT] ReviewTest executed. Required: reviewed server, build_check. | PHASE 4 — CREATE EVALUATIONS. Load reference/evaluation.md. Follow the 4-step process: (1) tool inspection — list the server's tools and their capabilities; (2) content exploration — use ONLY read-only / non-destructive operations (with limit<10, pagination) to explore available data, and do NOT read the MCP server implementation code; (3) generate eval_count complex, independent, realistic questions; (4) answer verification — solve each question to confirm a single string-comparable, stable answer.
EvalGen.step2: Ensure each authored question is Independent, Read-only, Complex (multiple tool calls), Realistic, Verifiable (single answer via direct string comparison), and Stable (answer will not drift over time). Frame answers as scalar string-comparable values, avoiding dynamic counters (reactions/replies/members) that change over time.
EvalGen.step3: sys.assert(every authored qa_pair requires ONLY tool calls whose readOnlyHint=true and destructiveHint=false — i.e. read-only, non-destructive, idempotent exploration — and any qa_pair that would require a WRITE or DESTRUCTIVE operation is flagged and DROPPED) -> enforces NN1. A qa_pair whose required tool path touches a write/destructive tool fails the assertion and is removed before emission.
EvalGen.step4: Emit the evaluation as XML: a single <evaluation> root containing one <qa_pair> per question, each with exactly one <question> and one <answer>. Write evaluation.xml into build_workspace. Pass the evaluation set + counts to ReportDeliver.
EvalGen.constraints: Evaluations are strictly read-only: NN1 (step3) forbids any write/destructive operation. Exploration uses bounded calls (limit<10, pagination) and never reads the server implementation code. Each <answer> is a single string-comparable, stable value.
EvalGen.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(emit the read-only qa_pairs that passed NN1, mark count PARTIAL) -> inform(User). Error types: assertion_error(write_or_destructive_qa)->drop the offending qa_pair, continue. parse_error(eval_xml_malformed)->retry(1) then partial. timeout(exploration_timeout)->retry with backoff.

ReportDeliver.step1: [ASSERT] EvalGen executed. Required: reviewed server, evaluation set, build_check. | ASSEMBLE the build_result per json_schema: language, transport, server_files[], tools_implemented[] (each with its four annotations + strict_input_schema + paginated flags), build_check (compiled / inspector_ok / stdout_clean), evaluation_xml_path, and evaluation_count. Set status=COMPLETE for a full pass or PARTIAL if any upstream node degraded.
ReportDeliver.step2: OUTPUT to user: a readable delivery report in the user's language — the generated MCP server file list, the per-tool annotation/schema/pagination summary, the build/test outcome, and the evaluation suite — plus the machine-readable build_result JSON. HONESTY DISCLOSURE: state which non_negotiables were structurally asserted (NN1/NN5/NN6/NN7/NN8/NN9 via sys.assert, NN10 via the tools allow-list) and reiterate that the four annotation hints are hints, not security guarantees. Note any PARTIAL/degraded steps honestly.
ReportDeliver.constraints: Output is a delivery report; it writes only into build_workspace and never modifies the bundled read-only references. PARTIAL status is surfaced honestly when any phase degraded. Reaches endNode.
ReportDeliver.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(emit build_result with degraded-fields warning) -> inform(User). Error types: assembly_error(schema_mismatch)->retry(1) then best-effort with warning. io_error(write_failure)->retry(1) then inform.

endNode.step1: [ASSERT] ReportDeliver executed. Required: build_result. | Terminal node: return the assembled build_result (generated MCP server + evaluation suite + build report) to the caller and end the run. No further computation and no modification of the bundled reference docs.
endNode.constraints: Final node. Pure return. Writes nothing outside build_workspace and never mutates source_material.
endNode.Error: OPTIONAL. inform(User) on any terminal anomaly.
